idiom_name: make(chan struct{}, N) - send to acquire, receive to release
implementation_notes: Go has no semaphore type because the language already has one: Effective Go states that a buffered channel can be used like a semaphore to limit throughput - make(chan struct{}, N) sets the ceiling, sending blocks when the buffer is full (acquire), receiving frees a slot (release), and the buffer capacity is the permit count. The classic counter-plus-waiters structure is replaced by the channel's own queue; add a select with ctx.Done() or default when acquisition must respect cancellation or fail fast, and keep the channel unexported and never close it.
pitfalls: Closing the channel makes every blocked sender panic instead of receiving a permit; a semaphore channel is never closed.
A bare send to a full channel blocks forever, so an overloaded server accumulates goroutines without bound unless a ctx or default case is present.
Channel capacity is fixed at make(); resizing a live bound requires a separate limiter (and golang.org/x/sync/semaphore.Weighted is fixed at NewWeighted too).

variants.name: golang.org/x/sync/semaphore.Weighted
variants.implementation_notes: When permits must be weighted (a request that needs k units) or acquisition must be cancelable, golang.org/x/sync/semaphore.Weighted is the packaged form: NewWeighted(n) fixes the capacity, Acquire(ctx, k) blocks until k units are available or the context is done, TryAcquire(k) is the non-blocking form, and Release(k) returns units - panicking on release more than held. Its waiter queue is FIFO, and a large request at the head of the queue blocks smaller ones behind it, which keeps big requests from starving.
pitfalls: Acquire(ctx, k) with k greater than the total capacity waits until the context ends; validate weights against the capacity instead of relying on the timeout.
Release() panics when it would take the held total below zero, so a double release crashes the process rather than silently widening the bound.
The weighted semaphore is not reentrant and has no fairness knob beyond its FIFO order; nested acquisitions of the same semaphore can deadlock.
